utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Could we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, please, my name is Niemann,. I appear with my colleagues, Ms. McHenry and Mr. Huber for the Prosecution, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: May we have the appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, my name is Edina Residovic, I am counsel for Mr. Delalic. My Co-counsel is Eugene O'Sullivan, professor from Canada. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Mr. Olujic and I am Counsel for Zdravko Mucic and together here with me today is Niko Djuric, an attorney from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My Name is Salih Karabdic, attorney from Sarajevo. I am here as a counsel to Hazim Delic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Nancy Boler. I represent Esad Landzo I am from Houston, Texas. My colleague, Cynthia McMurrey is working on a defence matter and she will be here later this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Residovic, I think you are still with your witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed. Examined by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Milic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I hope you had time to rest over the weekend and I hope that I need not to report the notice I told you on Friday. This is also valid today. But nevertheless, to repeat, would you please wait for the end of the interpretation then answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, you remember that on Friday, we concluded our conversation by your answer, which was that basis for your inspiration to work on the footage in question from one hand was due to a well orchestrated and efficient campaign in the Croatian media. And, on the other hand, certain facts that you were given from various sources, which gave you basis to start with a counter campaign. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this was so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will continue in the same direction with my questions. To one of my questions you partially confirmed. I would nevertheless like to have that clarified further. Did you, Mr. Milic, in any personal -- from any personal knowledge know facts and events in Konjic as well as did you know anything about the activities of Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I said on Friday that from the beginning of the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina and during the war I was not in Konjic, Sarajevo or any other part of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I was not a war reporter, I was not in the field in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I was then abroad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, did you personally put together all the commentaries on the footage and if you can remember how many of those were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My final version had 15 commentaries. And seems to me 22 edited excerpts. And I think we went through the tape yesterday again and the text read by the speaker who was not very skilful, but it is in accordance with what I wrote’ with what I created.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have told the Chamber that you were shown a tape by the Defence and it is a Defence exhibit. And even without my question, you confirmed to the Chamber that these were your commentaries. You have answered to my following questions at that. So my question now is, in this tape, which is accepted as exhibit, are there all your commentaries and excerpts or is there something missing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would like to view through the tape presented to the Chamber by the Prosecution. Again, because I know that on my version of the tape, my last words, were supposed to be in connection to Zejnil's arrival and the time he spent in Vienna and later on we put Zejnil's statement on the tape. And this is the tape that I put together and I claim it as my version. The version of the tape that the Prosecution holds I shouldn't -- I wouldn't want to comment on it right now. I would like to compare the two versions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will probably have time to return to that later on, but before we put your testimony in connection with the exhibit we have here, because the tape is not something that can be presented without viewing. You have to see it. But, nevertheless, could you tell us, do you know who edited the tape in Vienna when you gave the instructions for it? Do you know who made the final version?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but I can presume that it was one of the people that Dzemal or Ciso found in Vienna. But what is obvious is that it was done by amateurs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember, Mr. Milic, in which manner was the text read on that tape, the text submitted by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My judgement is that it is done very poorly, in a very amateur way. The only effective part refers to the introductory part of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, but this and a footage taken by the Konjic television. The camera and editing is too still, it's too dead, whilst we are listening to the speaker, the reading of the speaker is very bad. So they must have had poor technology and people who are amateurs who do not know their work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On Friday you said that you went quickly through 20 or 30 tapes and then that you viewed carefully the two tapes which you made out of those 20 or 30. And then, according to your directives, the final version was made. Can you remember what was the duration of the final tape that you have received from Vienna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Conditionally speaking it is a final version. I believe it was about three and three and a half hours. It is still a raw version. We wanted to have that up to 80 minutes, which is still too much. The point or the statement of that footage was supposed to be a certain basis which we would then use at various press conferences. But the version that came from Vienna could not be released to public in that duration. But, nevertheless, the operation stopped. I don't know the exact reasons for it, but that's the end of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we continue in this direction a bit. On Friday you said that you gave directions for the script and the draft. And when you said that, when you gave those directions, did you also offer suggestions about what has to be stressed in the excerpts that are to be left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that I asked from Dzemal, for Zejnil as the hero of my story, so to speak, to be in the first plan. He has to be on the screen for at least five seconds. But they took that too literally and then I had Zejnil up to five or ten minutes constantly on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The authenticated footage was on those 20 or 30 tapes, and then I made my version, edited version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I just wanted to clarify that. Mr. Milic, you said what your sources of information were and when you finally received the tape, you wanted to have the opinion of a person's that the tape was all about. Do you know whether this tape was shown to Mr. Delalic and, if so, who showed it to him and where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Quite a bit later after our work, I learned that Zejnil Delalic saw the tape, but that he decided not to proceed. Otherwise, I insisted that Zejnil sees the tape because I didn't directly want to tell those people that this is not what I wanted and that we should have to have consultations or Zejnil Delalic's opinion. Then through Dzemal, I asked to be given Delalic's opinion. At that time he was in Munich. And after awhile, Dzemal told me that they decided not to proceed. That Zejnil Delalic was grateful for my work and effort, but that he chose to seek compensation through attorneys. I was not happy with that decision, especially because at that time, time was on the Bosnian side, as well as on my and his side. But such is life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Within those 15 commentaries that you put together, did you describe Zejnil Delalic's activities during 1992 in a truthful way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only partially. Everything else was intended to be a counter campaign with only one aim to tell our people and the Croatian public that the undeniable truth is Mr. Delalic is not a Chetnik, he's not a KOS member, that he did not flee by using Chetnik helicopter. And that he did not betray the principles and the fight for Bosnia-Herzegovina. That Zejnil Delalic did not betray the siege of Sarajevo. And that he is not a person who released Serb detainees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To return to one part of your answers. On Friday you said that all the propaganda against Zejnil could have been put in three categories, one of them being that he's a KOS member, K-O-S, and that he aids the Serb sides and that he's trying to strain the relationship between Croats and Muslims. And the third, that he used the Chetnik helicopter to flee to the Serb side. Due to a better understanding of what you referred to, I wanted to ask you at the end of 1992 and beginning of 1993, what did it mean to be stigmatised as a Chetnik in a campaign undertaken in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could move even further. Generally speaking, in western Europe, if one is called "Chetnik" amongst Muslims or Croatians, literally meant a death sentence. Without any law or by using any methods possible, excluding Croatian population, which traditionally has certain hatred against Chetniks. At the same time in Croatia there were between 300,000 and 500,000 Bosnian Muslims who fled before the Chetnik knife. People who went through a lot at that period. Many of them still remember the Second World War and the term "Chetnik" by itself, even for the Chetnik himself, has a very, very negative conation and is a source of a lot of negative energy. And you can imagine what the situation is if one is being presented as a Chetnik amongst his own people. And this is what happened to Mr. Zejnil Delalic. This means to not only sentence you to death, but his entire family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Answer to my question, you have said not only in Croatia, but in the entire Western Europe, what would that mean if you can clarify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The public in Bosnia-Herzegovina during 1992, over 1 million of Bosniaks were in other countries like Switzerland, Netherlands, Austria and later on Sweden opened up its borders. And all those people did not have contact with the Bosnia-Herzegovina media, which were supposed to be the most reliable source of information. BiH television did not have its satellite programme. Radio transmission was destroyed by Chetniks and HVO. Our press did not arrive to those countries and people were thirsty for information. They didn't know the foreign languages, neither German or English or French. And, therefore, they were directed towards Croatian media, Croatian satellite channel and the Croatian press. I believe three dailies, three Croatian dailies were present in foreign countries and four to five weeklies, which dealt thoroughly with the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Thoroughly, of course, is under quotations because at that time we had the campaign going against Zejnil Delalic and some other members of the Bosnian TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that this additional clarification also explained a motive of your engagement with the tapes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the effort you invested in that work, was it rewarded? Did you have any benefit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that never went through entirely,. My work never really saw the light of day that I thought it would. And in that period of active cooperation and my work, we didn't have time to worry about fees, although it doesn't mean that I wouldn't have received anything. But at that time, I had money and Mr. Vesid and Dzemal were there when we would meet, when I would come to Zagreb, they would pay my round trip ticket and money that would be spent on food in Zagreb. That was all paid by then. But there was no agreement, written agreement about the whole deal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To return to the text that you put together, you said that the press stated that Mr. Delalic was a Chetnik and a traitor, in your commentaries, how did you try to present him to counter this campaign?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my comments, he had to be the absolute opposite. The absolute opposite of everything which they said he was. He was a patriot, he was a combatant, a humanist. And my commentary, men in the forefront of the fighting ranks for Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as you said on Friday, there was a very significant propaganda action being carried out, vis-à-vis Mr. Delalic saying that he was releasing the Chetniks. What did you advance to counter such a propaganda thesis in such a propaganda machinery in your own text?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, in order to boost the morale of the people and to watch this milieu of him, I was even, even more caustic in one of my versions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that a number of these attacks launched against him in the press was that he was against the lifting of the blockade in Sarajevo, and that because of that action of his, Sarajevo was even under a stronger blockade. So what did you offer in your text to counter such propaganda, namely, that he was against the lifting of the blockade of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to me, he was in the forefront of the ranks for the lifting of the blockade of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, I've confined myself in my questions to just what you have said, that was the fundamental basis of this campaign of yours, not every single caption that you used in this tape. Please tell me, as regards these facts which you have just enumerated, namely, that he was the organiser; that he was the bellwether, that he was in the forefront of the struggle for freedom; that he locked up Serbs; that he was the first to organise the lifting of the blockade of Sarajevo; Mr. Milic, did you hear these facts from persons to whom you talked, from Ciso, from Vejsil, from Dzemil, from Sefik, or did you hear that from other persons from Konjic, who at that time, were staying in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Now we are returning to an analysis of my own pattern of my own position. I believe it will suffice if I say that these were improvisations, my own improvisations. That was my story, which only had one objective, and that is to refute, at least in part, the effects to offset the effects of the Croatian propaganda campaign being waged against Zejnil Delalic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But still, Mr. Milic, I understand you have given me an indirect answer, but I should like to ask you to tell me, was one of the persons, did one of the persons whom I enumerated, personally tell you that Zejnil Delalic was the organiser of the struggle in that region, and that he locked up Serbs, and that he was the first person, the leader of the people, to lift the blockade of Sarajevo? Did any one of these persons tell you these facts, relate to you these facts as truthful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. On the contrary. In the time when I was making this tape, there was some reluctance on the part of Dzemal, actually objections raised on the part of Dzemal, in respect of some of my formulations. In respect of a specific operation, I'm not quite sure which one in relation to a village, when I put him in the forefront, and when I glorified him. He said that I was exaggerating, that this was a man who had rented two houses only and equipped a unit and participated in the -- putting together of some formations. And there was some sort of meeting, a consultation in the place Fojnica and, according to him, that was also an exaggerated report on my part. But, I repeat, everything was in pursuit of a single objective, this whole story. It had four-and-a-half typewritten cards of text and it required -- it would take some 15 to 16 minutes on the part of a professional announcer to read it on radio. So nicely put together and read properly, that would give the proper effect regarding Mr. Delalic's welcome in Vienna, which was the whole point, the, like, motive of this story. And that would also be reflected, would yield results in the field, that is to say in our own as well as in the Croatian public.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic (sic), when we started our conversation, I asked you about the programme called a picture -- "To Picture," which is a TV Zagreb programme, and you said, as is recorded in the transcript, that you did not see, but that you saw it later. Will you please tell me when you saw it and why was it important; why did you feel it was important for you to mention it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This question also leads us to an analysis of my text, which I still do not have as such, but I recall some things. I did say that a -- directed programme -- I did not see this programme that you referred to on television myself then, but I will be seeing it, I will be viewing it on the video cassettes which will come from Vienna. And the title, which Mr. Latin either deliberately or inadvertently, -- Mr. Latin -- was quite suitable for me. I could use it properly. They, namely, call him Mr. Delalic, the commander of the Territorial Defence of Konjic, I believe, what is -- essentially that he was a commander. Although he was not one. And Dzemal told me that Zejnil later wanted to deny that, but, as we lived quite quickly and worked quite quickly in that period, life simply went on. But I saw excellent material in it to project an image before our own public, that the cassette was originally intended for, offers Zejnil Delalic as a commander and to lay there by the foundations for all my theses in the text which was to follow, and which has some 160 typewritten lines of text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milic. Your Honours, in view of the fact that the witness is speaking about a specific Exhibit in this case, I should like to ask you, whether to be able to correlate this testimony with the Exhibit. I should like to ask the Prosecutor whether the evidence material contains this videotape, whether it is marked E46 -- I46 as a whole or partially so, because we have received both tapes under the same number and the decision of the court refers to I46. So if you could please clarify this for me, it would be easy for me to see whether the witness recognises this videotape as the one that he made comments for, namely, I am talking about evidence material, Exhibit number 116.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know whether it's the tape he is talking about or not. It's their witness, not ours. They have had opportunity to look at the video and make that decision themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Do you understand what Mr. Niemann said?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not, Your Honours, because when the Prosecutor proposed that 116 be tendered into evidence, he gave us two videotapes. One was an abridged version, and one was a whole version, as reportedly found in INDA-BAU, with the proposal that the text of the journalist should not be accepted. But by your decision you did accept the cassette videotape I46, which is Exhibit 116. So we did not know whether the Exhibit contains this cassette found in INDA-BAU or just the excerpts which the Prosecutor has also given us. So I just wanted the Prosecutor to clarify that particular fact for us, because your decision, actually, encompasses I46, but we have both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The evidence is about the tape your witness edited. That is the evidence he is giving. If that is the tape you want to tender, you go ahead and tender it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: May I then ask that cassette number 2, that this Exhibit contribution number 1, which is contained on a tape number 2, be shown, so that we can see whether the witness recognises it as his own work. Can we take this tape, which you have here, and give it to the technician?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is the Prosecutor's tape I46, which is Exhibit 116. It has been accepted on the 19th of January. There is a full transcript of the entire tape 16A and 16B, with excerpts from the transcript also given. Then we also have the transcripts of 116C, which was shown for another witness. Would you like cassette number 116?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (Microphone turned off) -- because he is only giving evidence of what he edited.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'd like the technicians to show us the beginning of this tape and the end of this tape. I assume that the Trial Chamber will appreciate that we do not have to watch the entire tape, which probably runs for some three hours. We just want to check whether that is the tape. Of course we can always view the edited parts, but may I now ask the usher to take the cassette to the technical service and to project, to show us the beginning, so that we could correlate this testimony of this witness with the evidence in question. If you'll allow that, Your Honours. If the technical service is able to show us this tape, will they show us the first report, which has been tendered into evidence and admitted by the court as Exhibit 116.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And may I ask you, Mr. Milic, to pay special attention to the text so that we could see whether the text is the text which you yourself prepared. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE  INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Before the beginning of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, a very small number of Muslims in Bosnia were ready for war. One of the few who reckoned that there will be war, after all, was Zjenil Delalic, a famous businessman, who after 20 years working in the west, returned to his native Konjic in March this year and formed immediately an underground war headquarters and equipped two modern houses for that purpose. He obtained all the initial equipment, starting with the money, which he brought with himself, which he used for the HVO of Konjic and Jablanica, which had already been formed. Most of the citizens of Muslims look at them as the opposers of the formidable JNA, the Serbs armed to the teeth. It was very clearly marked, which Serb sites had to be taken in the area of Konjic. The first operation of this kind was undertaken in the beginning of April, and the military factory Igman was taken with a great quantity of ammunition with which the entire Bosnia-Herzegovina was to use later for its war. At the Helm office, elected group of 20 lads in the night of 19 April. After midnight Zejnil took the Serb village of Celebici and the barracks in Celebici and the barracks in Celebici. That was the first seized JNA barracks in Bosnia-Herzegovina with a rich arsenal of war booty and ordinance, and this same group stationed themselves there as the first combat group on the Territorial Defence in Konjic right away. That 12 soldiers who were being released to go home via Split were the source of the anger of Mr. Kukanjac, and Kukanjac shouted how he would bomb Konjic in retaliation. This group attacked the 8th of April and took all the other barracks and the depot of Territorial Defence weapons and ammunition. During this operation General Kukanjac sent a whole squadron of aeroplanes, which succeeded to destroy more than half of the ordinance which belonged to Konjic, Jablanica, Prozor. And this is how it looked after the first bombing and shelling in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please now stop the projection of the tape. Mr. Milic, you heard this first text. Is this the text which you personally wrote yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, but perhaps because of some technical inadequacy, we do not have the credits, the television Konjic caption.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you didn't see, but it was shown.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. So this is the text which you wrote. Your Honours, can we now look at the end of this tape to see whether it is the end of the final version of the cassette which this witness had in his hands. So I should like to ask the technical people to show us the end of the cassette now. I believe that the technical section has understood that I would like to view a couple of minutes of the last part of this cassette, so that the witness could see whether it is a tape which he made. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: -- Detracting our attention from our main task, which is fighting the Chetniks. Zejnil is exerting maximum efforts so as to calm down tensions, but the HVO is trying to smear him as much as possible in every possible way. They are resorting in this effort to all sorts of conceivable things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, this is impossible to follow. Thank you. It's enough. Mr. Milic, was this the last part of the cassette which you edited, which you prepared? Please tell me, as this cassette which here is Exhibit number 116, which has been submitted by the Prosecutor to the Defence, have you had occasion to see this cassette? Tell me, at this point in time, now that you have seen these parts, were all your previous articles included in that cassette?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. But then there was this abrupt cutting off of parts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean? What was missing? How many of your reports or articles or segments of this text was missing? Can you remember exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After talking to Mr. Diva Caric (phoen) and Zejnil, please, I know that the last part which I wrote is missing, and that is the light motive of my report, of my story, and that is also a shot of Zejnil Delalic from the welcome ceremony in Vienna. And then there was after that something which was subsequently added by Dzemal to this cassette, which I know for a fact was produced by me. That part is the part of Zejnil's message, which did not fit into it, namely, it was not originally intended to be part of this material, but Dzemal had it produced and given to me for my inspection. But this message of Zejnil's was supposed to reach through some channels Sarajevo, the ^ Sarajevo people.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, given the fact that this witness has said that all the texts, from the first one to this one, are his indeed, but that there is one missing, if I understand the things right and if I can say this. If the Prosecutor agrees that these texts which are contained on the cassette, from the first to the penultimate text, according to the witness, I suggest -- I move that this be accepted, that this be admitted. If it is not admitted, then I propose that perhaps we should show every one of the texts of the parts of the cassette so that the witness could recognise them. Because there were 12 of them, as we know, and these ones which were mentioned by the witness too. So if the Prosecutor agrees, if we could perhaps accept this proposal of mine so that we don't have to view the entire cassette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (Microphone turned off) How about a suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have no objection to the tape being tendered. I can't give any assurances that it's the tape that was made in its entirety by this gentleman, this witness, but I certainly have no objection to it being tendered.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, it has been made part of the evidence. I just want the witness to confirm that the text of -- the journalistic text on the cassette actually belong to this witness. That is the whole point of his testimony. So what I am actually asking is whether the Prosecutor accepts that these texts are texts of this witness, namely, that we do not have to show every story to the witness for him to identify it as his own text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But has he seen the tape which is in the Court, the whole of it, this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the witness has seen this cassette.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He has seen all those 12 portions? Ask him if he's seen all those portions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, have you seen all these portions, from the first to the last, which was shown here right now? Do you recognise that as the text which you personally wrote?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those are my texts, but abridged. The whole video cassette has been abridged. It is not complete.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, you've just said that there is a commentary of yours missing and two stories, the one regarding the welcome in Vienna, which was very important to you for your whole effort, and the statement by Mr. Delalic. Your Honours, in order for us to be able to identify that part of the text also, in accordance with Rule 66 the Prosecutor has submitted to us cassette I66, which has the reportedly being found in INDA-BAU. So may I ask you that this text, which is also a continuation of this cassette, which is already in the evidence, I should like to ask you to let the witness view it. May I ask the usher to give you this text of the Prosecutor. I have a copy for the Prosecutor and for the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (Microphone turned off).

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is all, Your Honours, one cassette, but it was simply cut where his last story was, and that last story is contained in another cassette, which was allegedly found also in INDA-BAU and which the Prosecutor has submitted to us. I should like to show the witness's last segment to see whether that is also the story which this witness made when he made the original complete tape. So that is a part of the last segment. He did say that there were 15 texts, 15 stories, on the original cassette, and this one which was given to us contains 14. We've heard another witness explain to us the problems related to the editing of the text, so it is quite possible that there was a technical problem of that kind involved. I have here a translation of the text for you, and I should also like to ask the witness to take a look at it to tell us whether that is his concluding commentary. The Prosecutor did not offer as evidence that cassette, but only the first one, but he did submit the latter to us, to the Defence, for their inspection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document 184A.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I should now like to ask the technical people to let us see the first story from the first tape, the story with a flag.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will be listening to the text in our language, Mr. Milic, so that you don't have to look at the English version. It is tape number 1 and the first story on that tape. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My apologies, but I gave the written translation of the text. That's why there was no interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, is this the last story made by you when you were putting the tape together for the counter campaign for Mr. Delalic? Is this your last written commentary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The text read by the speaker is my last commentary, which was supposed to be illustrated by the footage from the club of his business associates in Vienna, which we saw only a brief second of. And I said already that on the final tape sent to me by Dzemal from Vienna, there was Zejnil's statement added for the Sarajevo public.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we now see for a minute another story from tape 1. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. This part is five to six minutes long. Can the technical service please interrupt the tape now, stop it. Either fast forward it or stop it because we've seen enough to ask the question I wanted. Mr. Milic, is this footage of the welcome reception that was in line after your final commentary in the final version of the tape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this was where the tape was supposed to end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would this footage then confirm your thesis that Zejnil Delalic did not use Chetnik helicopter to flee to the Serb side, but rather that he came to Vienna amongst his business and personal acquaintances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have mentioned that already a few times today, that the -- motive, the point of the entire idea was to prove that Zejnil Delalic did not betray Bosnia-Herzegovina, Bosniaks, that he's not a Chetnik or a KOS agent. And the last ten lines of text that I wrote points to that. And all that needed to be illustrated by this particular footage. That was supposed to be the end. And also, then, the basis for any future discussions and questions at press conferences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Dzemal, to your script added another story, which, together with this reception party, Zejnil Delalic wanted to be sent to Bosnia. Since you had that tape in 1993, can we now briefly see the third excerpt from Tape 1, so that the witness could give his opinion on it? (Videotape played)?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have the text, can we please stop the tape a minute, so that we distribute copies. We have here written translations of the spoken text. Can this be distributed to the Judges and the Prosecutor's office. This text could also be given to interpreters, so they could follow.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we now go back to the third excerpt on Tape 1 to be shown to the witness, so that I could ask the following question. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: That was the welcome, with typical Chetnik songs because they say I came with a Chetnik helicopter. This is really simple for some sick, imaginative imbeciles to fabricate because they are unable to show one fifth of my results in this stupid war.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe this is sufficient for me to ask the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, is that an excerpt added to your script by Mr. Delalic's brother, Dzemal, for which he said that Zejnil wanted to send it to Sarajevo together with the footage from the reception?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honourable Judges, since this witness needs to testify on the entirety of the tape, I would suggest that the text which the witness recognises is the final text of his tape, with two additional stories, which he also recognised as excerpts from 1993 be admitted into evidence for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is No. D-186. A for the first part, B for the second and C for the third part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If the person shown on the screen was your client?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You heard from the previous witness that in the fit of depression wanted to send that statement to Sarajevo. I cannot say more of it because I did not witness it. But since this particular witness had the tape in his hands, could confirm that. Mr. Milic, the Chamber has just admitted these additional parts which were missing, but could you please state again that all the written texts read on the previous tape between 1 and 14 are really your texts, is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely. Every speaker's word is what I wrote. I wrote that in Fontana, in Croatia in 1993, mid-March, I believe, sometime in the spring of 1993. That was the period of most intensive work. These are my words, my text, which, unfortunately, was not made public. It was disposed of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, the last commentary with the text of Mr. Delalic's leaving Konjic and his arrival to Vienna, was this the basic aim of your counter campaign, which was suppose to prove that Zejnil did not leave for Belgrade, but instead he came to Vienna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe on Friday and today, I stressed the light motive, the point and the aim we had. And exactly through this last excerpt we wanted to tell everything. That he's not a Chetnik. He's not a KOS agent. That he's not a traitor, but rather, that he's a son of Bosnia-Herzegovina and its people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the last thing I wanted to tell you before the Chamber referred to commentaries which were your journalist improvisation with an aim of counter campaign or a reaction to the propaganda seen in the Croatian press. So my question is, is this the essence of everything that you have spoken of here? Although many of those things referred to certainly are things that you cannot personally testify.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the essence. This is my work. I cannot say more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, I believe I clarified that, but my colleague warned me in full right. The witness confirmed several times that the text on this tape, as well as the text that we have shown now are his. Therefore, does the chamber accept that these texts were made by this witness and they form a part of the tape which is Exhibit 116?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I object to that, Your Honour. I believe that was clear, but...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is what this witness claims, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that was clear, but since my colleague warned me, I wanted to clarify that. Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness. Mr. Milic, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is there any cross-examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the second accused Defence has no questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Delic's Defence has no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BOLER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence of Esad Landzo has no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Niemann

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not Mr. Delalic, did you see any material that he had sent to other journalists other than yourself when you were preparing this tape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I am not familiar with that. Concerning the media of Croatia, Serbia and the TV Konjic and some footage were taken from our national B and H television. That was what the tapes I had consisted of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was really more or less just asking about written material that he had prepared, did you see anything of that nature, other than the section that he has just read out that is now being admitted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not have a single written material. I made my notes and I received information from Dzemal, Ciso, Vejsil and some other people. And I also taped some news from Croatian radio or Serb radio. I did not have written material, but I used Croatian media as the basis for my commentaries and I followed the reporting. I analysed it. I received something from Vejsil as well. And on the basis of their content and the given moment, I decided to put together the material as seen here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now when you're in Croatia at that particular time, did you ever hear of a news agency with the initials BIPA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. The official Croatian agencies here HINA, H-I-N-A.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It might not could not be Croatian, it could be somewhere from the former Yugoslavia, maybe Bosnia. Have you ever heard of a newspaper agency, B-I-P-A, BIPA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't pay particular attention. I never heard of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about a journalist by the name of Mr. Nosic, N-o-s-i-c?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard of Nosic in Latin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did Mr. Nosic, where did he come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know because I don't know him personally. I also believe he's not an influential name in the journalistic community, so I didn't pay too much importance to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me what you do know about him and how is it that you know his name and what you do know of him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely nothing in particular, maybe I came across one of his texts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any of material sent to Mr. Nosic by Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it Mr. Nosic was in Croatia, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can assume for yourself, but I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you've heard of his name, so you must have heard of his name in connection with some place or another, surely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During an ordinary day, I would go through four or five Croatian dailies, at the same time listening to the radio and television. And if I am concentrated on the content, I do not think of who wrote a particular text. My motto and what I also realise is that here we dealt with an organised, orchestrated campaign by all the media. I paid attention to some of my colleagues names, colleagues from Bosnia-Herzegovina. And by that time they were also moving slightly towards the side which was on the way to betray the Bosnia principles. I may have come across Mr. Nosic's name. But I don't know anything more about him. I remember, for example, texts by Zlatko Prlenda. And he was one of my editors in Sarajevo. And also one of the people I corroborated with. And his texts were published in Slobodan Dalmatia, and we can talk about him, for example. But as concerns Mr. Nosic, his name doesn't mean anything to me. I may have, in some of the Croatian press, whether in Slobodan Dalmatia, Vetchna, Vijesnik (phoen) or some magazines, or in Globus (phoen). Or paper published in Istria. So at those instances, I could have come across his name or his initials, but that's all I know of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I think that you said in your evidence that you prepared this material so that you could organise a campaign to bring to the light of the day what actually did happen in Konjic and to counter the propaganda that was being perpetrated especially against Mr. Delalic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I have already said that and I state now that in my propaganda material, I wanted to counter negative effects from Mr. Delalic and Bosniaks in general. And these effects were caused by well-organised campaign launched at exactly a particular moment through the Croatian media.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the attacks on Mr. Delalic perpetrated entirely by Croatian media or were they also media in Bosnia-Herzegovina that was attacking Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not one of the Bosnia-Herzegovina mediums had anything negative concerning that. There were a certain number of Bosnia media which could be listened to or bought in Croatia, if we're talking about radio or the press. But they would mainly report on the successes of the defenders of Konjic or attempts of people to lift the siege of Sarajevo. But Zejnil Delalic was not mentioned often on Radio Sarajevo, which was my main source of information. Concerning B and H press, during that period there was no mention of his name. And the press at that time could not be found in Croatia. It cannot be found even today in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So far as you are aware at the time and that you have nothing to suggest otherwise, he was not receiving any adverse publicity or media comment in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The witness had said that he did not have that press.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not have it and I cannot precisely answer to your question. I told you I was not in the field and Bosnia-Herzegovina press could not be found in Croatia. And even today one cannot buy it in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you said that you also decided to exaggerate some parts of the script, did you exaggerate or just lie?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both. Both, exaggeration and lying. But I stress because I was instigated by other people's lives, by people who are my professional colleagues, people I attended university with, people that I used to have drinks and go out in Sarajevo before the war. Of course this is contrary to the profession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Microphone not on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Apparently that has credence in some marriages, it's not one I subscribe to myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, how did you expect to bring out the truth, the light of day, by lying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before you repeat the question, because I do not understand it properly. But in 1992 and 1993, when the Belgrade television issued up to 99 per cent of lies about how the Serbs are endangered in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the total picture was one big lie. So the foreign institutions at that time did not react. And at a certain point you've had enough of it and you go over your principles, your moral principles, your professional ethics, because what is in question are your people, are your country.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you have no intention --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And my family and myself were in a foreign country. But could you now repeat your initial question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, my initial question is, how could you possibly hope to bring out the truth which was your objective if you're going to do it by a process of telling lies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sir, they were not absolutely all lies. You must know that Zejnil Delalic was made a hero by the Croatian media. It is also a fact that Mr. Delalic, Zejnil, did come to Konjic in March, 1992. And that he said there for a while. He came there because of a tragedy in his family. It is a fact that he joined the defensive forces of the Territorial Defence force of Konjic. It is a fact that as a businessman, he donated equipment and uniforms to our defensive force members. For me, that is material enough to exaggerate some things. Always in the pursuit of the single objective offsetting and refuting much graver accusations against his person would smear him and, in fact, convicted him in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think the Trial Chamber will now rise and reassemble at noon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, you may proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Remind the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Remind the witness he is still under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I should like to remind the witness that you are still testifying under oath. Cross-examined by Mr. Niemann:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Milic, you mentioned the Belgrade media and what they were doing during the course of the war. I take it, that none of the campaign that you were engaged in was directed to anything that was being said about Mr. Delalic in the Belgrade media?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the period starting with 1992, the period that I had been in Croatia, I could not have access, direct access to any media to Yugoslavia from Serbia, apart from some contributions, some articles which were just given by way of illustration. In some programmes on Croatian television, or rather in the programme called "Picture by Picture" on Croatian television, those are the only things I could see. And that is not relevant to the period in which I spent in Croatia. What I mentioned had to do with a campaign in which all Serbs were to be mobilised to put up a maximum of defence campaign which sought to project an image of all Croatians as Ustashes, all Croatians on the soil of the former Yugoslavia, and all Muslims on the soil of the former Yugoslavia as Muslim fundamentalists, and as for Slovenians, they were to be shown as people who just lost their way and happened to be just come across Yugoslavia. Macedonians were spared of this image.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the allegations that you say you want to contend was the issue of the releasing of Serb prisoners from the Celebici camp. How did you know whether or not Mr. Delalic could or couldn't release Serbs from the Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know for a fact that, according to what Dzemo said, he had no particular special connections with this camp at Celebici. And my comment, my commentary, was precisely a response to the Croatian campaign. And it is a product, the lie, the Croatian lie, that he released Serbs in order to gain a specific image in Croatian, to project an image of him in the Croatian public. So I responded by -- this is where I say that he was arresting them, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the video doesn't mention that, does it, anything about the issue of releasing Serbs, your video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we would perhaps have to view it. I believe that there is a segment which says something about it. I think that there is a picture, a shot, some footage, a talk with Serb prisoners, namely, where they speak about the conditions of their stay at the prison. And I have to admit, when I saw this footage -- the footage was made, by the way, by BiH television. I believe it was Jadranka Milosevic. I was embittered, because she had given them so much room to speak after Ormarska and Manjaca. I was also bitter at the way they looked. I don't think they looked any worse than we here look, whereas I had the images of Ormarska and Manjaca in mind, and they conjured up very bitter feelings in us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the scenes about Celebici don't speak of the issue of Mr. Delalic, whether or not he was releasing Serb prisoners, from what I can see, anyway. Unless you tell me something differently. I believe there is a section about where Serb prisoners are interviewed, but there is nothing there discussed about whether Mr. Delalic could or couldn't release prisoners.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but, sir, the end of November, 1992, December, 1992, until the end of January, and perhaps the entire month of January, 1993, and all the available media arsenal in Croatia was used to correlate the name of Zejnil Delalic with the release of Serb prisoners. That is the cause why -- excuse me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It may well have been, but you didn't counter it. That's the point I am trying to make. Did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat that, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Croatian media may well have been directed against Mr. Delalic, because he released Serb prisoners, but you didn't counter it? Where did you counter it? I'm asking you where you did it. You point to a section where Serb prisoners are interviewed, but that doesn't deal with it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But, sir, this Croatian anti-propaganda, that is the propaganda against Zejnil Delalic, is something which I wished to neutralise, to eliminate. So I constructed my own sentences, my own section of the text where I projected a quite different image of Zejnil Delalic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were trying to project an image about Mr. Delalic that he was not favourable towards the Serbs. That was one of your objectives, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yet the only part of the Celebici footage that we see in the video is a short excerpt where the prisoners are saying how the conditions in Celebici were fine, were good. The food was good, they had three meals a day. That's hardly anti-Serb, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree that it's probably a lie, but it's not anti-Serb, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you are trying to -- if you are trying to produce an image that Mr. Delalic was not favourably disposed towards the Serbs, it hardly helps your campaign to put in a segment where the Serbs are saying how wonderful Celebici is, and what the food and conditions are like, are so wonderful, which is what is said. Witnesses are saying they get three meals a day and conditions are fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I object Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: -- partly is true and partly exaggerated. This is his stand, it is partly true and partly exaggerated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I object, Your Honours. The witness spoke about the text which he wrote, and he also spoke about the various stories and the way they were edited.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't see why I have to comment on other peoples stories. I can and I want to comment on, and I keep returning to, and I am trying to say to you that, in the absence of other stories, because there was a lack of other stories, we used this one, which perhaps would not have found a place in the final version of the cassette. But I want to highlight my own portion of the text in which I say that Zejnil Delalic set up prisons for Serbs, and I say that in order to defend him from the smear campaign which was being waged against him in Croatia at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, I don't know -- it depends on the way you look at the nature of this subject matter, whether it's anyhow perverted of any of the counts which Zejnil Delalic is charged.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It's a direct attack on the Austrian documents, Your Honour. It's directly attacking them, saying that they can't be believed. It runs somewhat counter to the Prosecution case. That's the reason for the cross-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: And while it's admitted that this is put as exaggerated and false in parts?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am not questioning that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell me what parts of the -- specifically, what parts of either your commentary or the films that you included, the video clips that you included, tell me specifically what parts of them were lies, so we can clarify that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can we please take the video cassette and then start from sentence by sentence, from the first to the last, story by story. Because you must bear with me, sir, even if you yourself had to analyse something that you wrote yesterday, you would not accept to do it. And I certainly cannot do it with something which I wrote in 1993 in this place. So I need to see the entire video cassette, from the first to the last sentence, to analyse it one by one for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just tell me about your highlights. You saw it on the weekend, you told us, you wrote it yourself, you are likely to know more about it than anyone else here in this courtroom. When it comes to telling a lie, it takes quite a bit of an effort to tell a lie, so you must know the highlights. You tell us which ones are the main lies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, but a specific question requires a basis, so that the witness might know what he is being asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: But the witness said the whole theme of the videotape consists of exaggerations and lies. All the Prosecution is asking for, what do you think a lie is, and what do you think exaggeration is? I think it's fairly easy for anybody to know which of them is a lie and which of them is exaggerated. He need not speak of all of them. He can speak of those he remembers. That should be enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness has answered my questions as to the lies which he has said, so I thought that that perhaps should be drawn attention to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: (Microphone off)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Let me just make something clear. What lies -- what lies are there in my text? What are lies? What are the lies in my text? That is what you are asking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I want to know, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I exaggerated at the very start, when I said that Zejnil Delalic had come and formed a defence headquarters, an underground defence headquarters. The truth is that he came for the funeral of his late brother --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (No microphone)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let him complete his answers before you interpose. Kindly complete what you regard as exaggeration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So the truth is that because of the scourge, the misfortune which befell our homeland, he joined the defensive forces of our Army. And the truth is that he is big businessmen, well-known businessman on the soil of the former Yugoslavia, generally, and that he is well-liked by the people, by our people, as a great humanitarian worker. The truth is that, de facto, he spent all that time in the field, and that he took occasional trips to Zagreb; that he worked as a charitable humanitarian worker; and also partly joined in the struggle. It is also true that taking the itinerary, as described in my last text, he reached Vienna. That is true. Everything else is my superstructure, additional constructions, my exaggerations and my interpretations. And if you analyse the entire text, with more attention from the first to the last word, then it sounds quite fine and effective, chronologically observed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you often lie professionally, or just habitually?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So that is a private question, a question I view as private, and I cannot answer. I have the right not to answer. But as regards this particular material, I lied deliberately and consciously in order to refute the lies of others which inspired me in my propaganda work. And, please, bear in mind the terminology used, a lie and the propaganda, two different things, two different specific gravities. And I should like us to speak on the subject of propaganda, not lies, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the last segment that we saw on television, where Mr. Delalic was speaking himself, and reading it out, which we saw as now Exhibit 185. The text of that, you didn't write that, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was a part that was attached to the video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, in fact, Mr. Delalic did participate in the making of the tape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did Mr. Delalic request you to exaggerate and lie himself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, sir, if you follow the course of the conversation we had today and the one on Friday, I never had any contact with Mr. Delalic, Zejnil, in that period. It was through Dzemo that I found out that Zejnil Delalic was not happy with my work, and the involvement of his family, and that he said that he was grateful, that he thanked us, but that he had decided to seek legal redress to the entire situation, this whole injustice -- in relation to all the injustice and all the evil with had been done him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Dzemal Delalic, or Mr. Ciso, did either of them tell you you should lie or exaggerate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. On the contrary, they actually sought to restrain me, to talk me out of it. After the first working version was prepared, after I had prepared it, then they drew attention to me, where I had exaggerated things, where I did not portray faithfully the situation in the field, but having the material available, in front of me, the HTV material, the Croatian television material that is, and having my own objective in mind, I myself decided to formulate the text in the way you have it before you today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you told Mr. Dzemal Delalic and Mr. Ciso to prepare the video clippings, did you instruct them to lie and exaggerate in the way it was to be presented?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir. No. I had no reason to do that. Especially because they said that they had many, many of those shots, clippings, and I asked them to bring as many as possible to me, so that I could use them for illustration purposes. I had not addressed any special requests at that period. The only thing which I asked them to do is when it came to the -- too long, the anaemic, the still life scenes to be eliminated, then this man, who was practically convicted and smeared in the public and gravely accused, I wanted him to be shown in the forefront. I wanted the camera to show him in the forefront. And they took me literally. So they had them speaking there for five or ten minutes at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That's all I have, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just one question. Was this tape shown on any television ever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. In fact, I don't know what came of it after this time, after the time I gave it last to Vejsil, what happened to it, where it went. I really have no idea, absolutely. Basically, it is an abortive project of mine, an incomplete project of mine, and I regret the fact that it has been abused in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ekrem. We are very grateful for your assistance. I think that is all for you. You are discharged. You can go. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Do we have another witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this morning we submitted to you a written submission to the Trial Chamber, and despite all our efforts we were unable to provide a witness -- one witness over this week. In addition to what I have written, I have received two fax messages from Sarajevo, in the television of Bosnia-Herzegovina, informing me that the persons supposed to appear as witnesses are unable to do so because of their professional commitments, so that they cannot come and appear before the Trial Chamber this week. In addition to everything which I have said and written in our written submission, and in view of these faxes which I received this morning, I could give you additional information, but, please, bear with me and appreciate the fact that Mr. Delalic's Defence Counsel has done everything in order to follow the instructions of this Court. So may I now ask the usher to show you these two faxes which I received this morning, so that these people should be relieved of their obligation to appear before this Court this week, because they are unable to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, have you any comments on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, we don't have any comments, Your Honours. We are ready to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, how many of the witnesses indicated here are unable to come? Because you have over seven witnesses left. I see there are -- how many of the witnesses -- only two here who cannot come. So you still have outstanding many other witnesses --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have three witnesses out of seven on this list because after all of our attempts, today we managed to get these two faxes and this was their response to our request, although my colleagues in my office in Sarajevo are trying to get in contact with another three witnesses and their employees, to get a permission to leave. And until now, we still did not receive their employer's answers. Last week we interrupted Mr. Alic's business trip, together with two people from Austria. Few people managed to change their schedules. So far, as I said, for two people, we have received faxes this morning. And the remaining three still did not give their final response because we suspect they will remain unable to change their professional obligations until the 22nd of June. And they all would be available after the 16th when this witness is to return from the United States. And our witnesses are at disposal of the Court on the 16th already. But this week we cannot bring anybody. Maybe we could transfer that to the next week because from what we received, nobody can come before the 16th. And only a week after that we could start calling up our witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This was not the information you had before now. What I am saying, at the time you indicated you're unable to call any of these witnesses, you did not have reasons why they could not come, other than they are professionally engaged somehow. But not with respect to all of them. This is what I mean. Those who are not so engaged could have come and you could have left out those who are so engaged, those who have official records to tender. And all those who you perhaps you got, and not involved in their professional duties and what professional duties not stated. That has understated. So we can find that you have not even given sufficient reasons why the Trial Chamber should exercise this discretion. Perhaps you took a very different view as to why adjournment must be granted. An adjournment is a discretionary remedy. And there should be valid reasons why such an adjournment should be granted. And you can see from your own position that you did not give any reasons whatsoever, other than professional engagement which people have. How can a Trial Chamber, without knowing what the professional is, go out exercising a discretion on behalf of a witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you allow. As you know, we planned a list of 54 witnesses and we contacted all the managers in the companies where those witnesses work. And all the commanders of the unit if they're in the military. And we had scheduled dated July 15th. But following your instructions, we reduced the list for 20 people and then we shortened our questions. We put them down to a fewer number, so that you would not think that we do not take your suggestion seriously. And the schedule that we had with managers and commanders of brigades has been significantly changed. And when I saw that we would have an empty period, we put our maximum efforts to press on some other witnesses and for five of them we have managed to, and we have seen them before the Court until today. But from what you can see here, three people can not come due to reasons I have stated. And then the one person from the archives cannot be available before the 12th, but that fax I have not received yet. There's an additional person who is a soldier and we do not have the army's permission for him. We have done everything in our power. There are two people and we spoke with their employers and we arranged that they would come at the beginning of July. We approached their employers to enable their employees to come earlier to the Court. But we have not received their answer in a written form. I can only convey that to you in an oral way. We haven't received faxes which would confirm that. But we are doing our best. We reduced the list, which saves significant amounts to the court. And if during the day I receive anything additional for anybody, we will forward that to you, but we did not receive any official document. I do not wish to obstruct the plans or life of a witness, but at the same time I try to meet the requests of the Chamber. And I also believe that you have accepted many proposals done by the Prosecution. I approached the Chamber again because I hoped that you would be able to understand that these witnesses are of crucial importance for our Defence. That Mr. Delalic would be punished if they were not given an opportunity to testify about the facts which are relevant to his Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: -- to be exercising professional judgement. When you have witnesses who have agreed to testify and you find it difficult to get them to come here on their own, except with the consent of their employers, as Counsel, you should know what to do. And if you have failed to do that which is good and in the interest of your clients, then you're failing in your duties towards your client and that is sufficiently negligent for any Counsel. I have watched and observed the way you've conducted this question of these witnesses. Your first reaction was to give a blanket reason and all professionally engaged and cannot come before that you have named. That was the approach. That is the first thing you did. Now one of the custodians of records -- I don't know which of them because there are two here -- is unable to come. What of the other one? If from the beginning you knew these details. You knew how each witness was engaged or had difficulties in coming. Counsel should know what to do to break through such difficulties and force the hands of their players to release a person. But I suppose you had other ideas, not seriously wanting them to come. Because you would not come on the 8th to ask for these witnesses to come. Nobody does that. At least no counsel. And here I put counsel in its proper context, should do that. Because all you are doing is to tell the Trial Chamber to refuse your application. Because there's nothing we can do about this. Even if we granted your application, it would not mean anything. Because you have been dealing with these witnesses for a long time. And you should have known their problems and should have known to learned how to correct these difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we scheduled our witnesses according to the testimony plan put together by the Chamber. If a witness goes on a business trip to the United States, that is not something we can do there. I would like it best that we, if we could have those people here and we did everything in our power for the situation to be so. I don't know where Your Honours get this impression that you would want to stall the proceeding. Two months ago, we asked whether the custodians of record could wrap up their work, but they have not. All the witnesses have wished to come, but they cannot. You've heard of what they think of subpoenas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If you look at one of these witnesses who is unable to come, is coming to give evidence in respect of conditions in Celebici. These are matters in respect of which you've been calling witnesses. If you knew he's unable to come about now, why did you call them all here? In which case they would not be in your way. Because that evidence you have led in respect of some cases. Some other witness have given evidence in respect of certain things. And this is why when I make a comment, I do not make it without supporting facts. I have my reasons why I make that. Because I say very experienced Counsel, you have an overview of evidence of all your witnesses. And you know what each is coming to say. Clearly, there's no question of telling us now that after some time this witness will now come to say what some other people have said, perhaps in a better way. I don't know, you know your case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is interesting. You are asking us to wait to the convenience of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You're telling the Court to wait to the convenience of the witnesses. This is a very interesting position to take.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. We gave an alternative suggestion. This witness in question, he was on a seminar in Washington and has been there since the half of May. And I knew that he would be here on the 16th. But had we not given up the 20 witnesses, he would have been here at the time beginning of June. So we planned that we also at that time call up the custodian of record. And by your suggestions, we reduced the number of witnesses. I believe this is also in the Defence's interest not to repeat things. But this poses a new obstacle to us. Because from this courtroom we could not react in any other way, which would be more efficient. We have brought five people who were planned to come later. But with these five, we did not manage to deal with the problems of other witnesses who could, according to the schedule, come only come in July. But now we can now see that they cannot be here before the 16th. This was not a mistake on the part of the Defence or the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You tendered your reply to the Prosecution's request for your list of witnesses. Have you seen your reply? It's not a question of inability to get them, to get your witnesses. The only reason there was that you've appealed against a ruling and, therefore, you could not give a list of witnesses. Not because your witnesses cannot be called. I hope I am not wrong in interpreting any way I have done. You look at your response. The 5th of June, that was your response to the Prosecution's request for a list of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is possible that we responded to the Prosecution, but I have stated the same arguments as I am stating today to you before you made your decision. And this was also mentioned in the appeal on the sequence of calling up witnesses. So this was always the arguments connected to the professional inability, professional schedule of witnesses to come and we couldn't influence it. We did our best to adjust our plan to the Chamber.
