So my arguments from before are written appeal and what we are approaching you with today are based on the same reasoning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Not the position in your -- list of witnesses dated 2nd of June. The list of witnesses, it's to 14. And the ones you say cannot appear because of professional duties or professional engagements. Now when I looked at it at that time, it did not even specify which of them it was against. It was a blanket condition for all of them. But I know that's not possible. It cannot be all of them. If at that time you knew only one, two, three or so are those who are engaged, what of the other ones who were not so involved? They too could not come. This is the assumption you had. That because three cannot, the others also could not. That is not the way to treat a Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, if you understood me that way. All 14 were unable to come. But in the meantime, through family connections, we found Mr. Alic in Austria and he could interrupt his professional duties for awhile and come here. And then also Mr. Velic, whose wife recently passed away, we persuaded him to come here as well as two people from Austria. All 14, I repeat, did have obligations, but five of them were able to change circumstances and appear before the Chamber. But for all the others, until at this moment, we were unable to. And we have an official report for three and for the other three we are missing an official report. But we did our best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic is in custody.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I do know, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: People who are unable to give up their professional engagements in the interest of someone who is in custody. This is a more important thing. He's in custody,. He wants his case closed, so that you know what else to do. And we've already applied to the Trial Chamber as to how to organise his Defence in respect of closing it and then making a submission. You've done that. Then why do these questions arise about people who are unable to come? Can't you see the conflict between that desire to expedite trial and the possibility of your witness coming to testify? When we should expedite a trial, you give yourself, the Prosecution and for the Trial Chamber to decide the procedure to be adopted. At the same time you're not getting your witnesses here, so that the case will be closed. And the procedure you are advocating should be adopted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It might look contradictory to our... But since the beginning of the separation of proceedings, we wanted to expedite the proceeding as much as possible. But between a quick and a fair trial, there's a difference because we would need only several days for these few witnesses. And this would be crucial for the Defence to hear what they have to testify about. And this is in the best interest of my client, especially because like some of them like, Byron Deric (phoen), provided us with a tape which was submitted and accepted as evidence concerning the conditions in the camp in Celebici. And they're important so you get a picture of the real truth. And they are in the best interest of the accused. And the Prosecution was also in a similar position. And then they would approach us, the Defence, to have an understanding for the obstacles they had in bringing their witnesses, which we did, we met their request. And this would be in the best interest of the Defence. And I plead to you that this time you would have an understanding for us and within the three days, we might be able to listen to testimonies of all those witnesses. If somebody calls me up and tells me that the witness could come here tomorrow, we would be happy to have that. But there was no way. I spoke to my colleagues in my office in Sarajevo and out of all the requests we sent to employers, we received only three. For one of them it is stated he is unavailable until the 12th of July and I do not intend to wait for him until then. We will then skip that witness. But there are certain witnesses who could come earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: I was just wondering if the football final was more important than the proceedings in this Court. I was just wondering.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I cannot comment on that. We have an alternative request. If we think that this particular witness should be here, we would ask of you to issue a subpoena. But in the sense of amicus curiae, what does it mean for people who wish to come in our conditions? You've heard five witnesses who were delivered a subpoena. They all wanted to come even without it. But the issue is whether they can come at the time appropriate for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Okay, we give your ruling after the break at 2.30 when we reassemble. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.55 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I indicated when we were rising that we'll give a short ruling now in respect of the arguments and we'll follow this up with a more comprehensive ruling. Now, this ruling is on the submission brought by Ms. Residovic on the alternative request for renewed consideration of Delalic's motion for adjournment until the June 22nd, 1998, or a request for issue of subpoenas to individuals, and request for assistance to the Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Now , this morning -- I think this motion was filed this morning. It was proceeded by the motion on the 2nd of June where, in the list of witnesses to be called, Counsel indicated that the witnesses numbers 8 to 14 will be unable to attend to testify, because they have indicated their inability to travel to The Hague before the week 22nd to the 26th June. Counsel was aware that the current witnesses for the accused, who listed first to seven, were likely to conclude giving the evidence not later than Monday, the 8th of June. The Trial Chamber's task, which is revising the lists submitted on the 2nd June, rejected the application and told Counsel to continue with the list of witnesses without interruption. The application for adjournment was rejected. Counsel was told, clearly and firmly, to close the case of the accused at the conclusion of the last available witness. On the 3rd June, Counsel gave notice of appeal against the decision of the Trial Chamber. On the 4th of June, the Prosecution filed a motion seeking disclosure of the names of the witnesses of the first accused. On the 5th of June, the first accused replied that, in view of the notice of appeal filed, there is no obligation to give such notice 'til after the termination of their appeal. The application filed this morning before the Trial Chamber seeks, (a), adjournment 'til 22nd, June '98, and (b), request to issue subpoenas to individuals and to the Government of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It is interesting to observe that the grounds for adjournment is that the witnesses for the accused are unable to reschedule their commitments to be able to appear in the Trial Chamber for the 22nd to 26th of June. This is an insufficient reason to support the application for adjournment. Counsel is familiar with the case of the accused, knows the witnesses and their testimony. Counsel had sufficient time to organise its witnesses, consistent with their private engagements. It is clearly not for the Trial Chamber to wait for their convenience, except where this is justified by the circumstances. The witnesses sought to be called have been known to cancel for quite a long time, and their commitment should have been known and taken into account in the calling of witnesses. Counsel is only today applying for subpoenas for witnesses to appear. There is no list of the names of witnesses or why subpoenas should be issued. Counsel has not disclosed that witnesses cannot appear to give evidence without the issue of subpoenas. We also asked for request for assistance under Article 29 of the Tribunal Statutes through the Government of Bosnia-Herzegovina for assistance. There is no evidence that that government has been approached for assistance and she has refused to do so. It is well settled that the granting of an adjournment is exercise of a judicial discretion. A Trial Chamber being approached for the exercise of that distraction must be giving credible reasons why the application should be granted. I examined the reasons given by Counsel and find no basis on which it could exercise a discretion to grant both the adjournment sought and the application for the subpoenas. We reject the application. Now, as it is, Counsel should know what to do, and we call upon Counsel to decide to close its case. I am following up with this. We expect Counsel for the second accused to call evidence in respect of the second accused on the 22nd of June. We've already lost the whole of this week because of what I regard as ineffectiveness in Counsel trying to put forward its witnesses, but we expect Counsel for Mucic to lead evidence from the 22nd of June. Thank you. I think this is all we have for the day and nothing more. So the Trial Chamber will now rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: 2.50 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, on the 9th day of June, 1998, at 10.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
